summary_html: **Educators/school staff** observing indicators of abuse/neglect report to CPS under state mandatory-reporter lists built on the federal CAPTA floor.
authority_html: - **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — requires robust reporter regimes that include education sector professionals

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Law Court vacated judgment on the pleadings for a child protective caseworker, holding that where the complaint alleges she interviewed and physically examined a child at school without parental notice, acted beyond her statutory authority, and acted with malice, Maine Tort Claims Act immunity could not be resolved on the pleadings.
key_cases.relevance: The interview and examination took place at the child's school without any notice to his mother and stepfather.
key_cases.quote: At a minimum, however, plaintiffs' complaint alleges that defendant acted beyond the bounds of any statutory authority she might have, and that she acted with malice.

key_cases.case_name: Hatch v. Department for Children, Youth & Their Families
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
key_cases.holding: The First Circuit held that the Constitution allows a caseworker to take temporary custody of a child without a hearing on an objectively reasonable suspicion that abuse has occurred or is imminent, and affirmed because the information the caseworker had, including a school report and a physician's hold, met that standard.
key_cases.relevance: The report originated with a school nurse's and teacher's observations relayed by the principal, the classic educational-disclosure trigger.
key_cases.quote: Because the welfare of the child is paramount, an objectively reasonable suspicion of abuse justifies protective measures.

Emergency medical services personnel — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Dentists, dental hygienists and dental assistants — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Chiropractors and podiatrists — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Registered and licensed practical nurses — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Teachers, guidance counselors and school officials — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
School bus drivers and school bus attendants — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Youth camp administrators and counselors — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Child care personnel — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Social workers and medical or social service workers — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Homemakers and home health aides — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Psychologists and mental health professionals — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Court-appointed special advocates and guardians ad litem for the child — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Law enforcement officials — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
State and municipal fire inspectors and municipal code enforcement officials — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Commercial film and photographic print processors — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Clergy members acquiring the information as a result of clerical professional work, except information received during confidential communications — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)

Humane agents employed by the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Sexual assault counselors and family or domestic violence victim advocates — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(A)
Any person who has assumed full, intermittent or occasional responsibility for the care or custody of the child, whether or not paid — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(B)

Any person affiliated with a church or religious institution who serves in an administrative capacity or has otherwise assumed a position of trust or responsibility to its members, while acting in that capacity — 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1)(C)
reporting_details: Maine is not a universal-reporting state: the adults listed in 22 M.R.S. § 4011-A(1) must immediately report to the Department of Health and Human Services when they know or have reasonable cause to suspect that a child has been or is likely to be abused or neglected or that a suspicious child death has occurred, and any other person may report voluntarily under § 4011-A(3).
